subject: SOC 2: supplemental artifacts request — MFA revocation proofs & keystore evidence
messages:
From: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@pulsehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@pulsehealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 artifacts: MFA revocation and keystore rotation evidence

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. PulseHealth is kicking off a brief re-evaluation ahead of our procurement review and we need a few supplemental artifacts in addition to your SOC 2 Type II report to complete our evidence package. Can you provide the following by EOD Tuesday (2026-06-16)?

- A bridge letter if the SOC 2 period in your Type II report does not cover March–May 2026 (we need a statement of controls continuity or interim compensating controls).
- A time-sliced export of authentication events showing MFA revocations (token revocation/disable events) for 2026-03-01 through 2026-05-31. CSV is preferred; include column headers and timezone info.
- Keystore/key-rotation manifest showing key IDs, rotations, and timestamps covering the last 6 months.
- Evidence of quarterly privileged access reviews for admin roles (PDF snapshot of the checklists/audit trail).
- A 1–2 page plain-English explanation of how revocation is guaranteed (what steps happen when a token is revoked).

If any of these items require an NDA or have IP constraints, let me know; we can accept redacted samples for the logs as long as the fields we ask for remain intact. Our security team is on CC — they may follow up with a narrow question set.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Lowe
IT Security Manager, PulseHealth
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 artifacts: MFA revocation and keystore rotation evidence

Hi Hannah — great to connect yesterday. Thanks for the clear list. Quick plan and owners below so you know what we will deliver and when: 

- Bridge letter (if required): Draft by 2026-06-16, final sign-off from Legal by 2026-06-18. Vanessa (me) will route for signature.
- MFA revocation slice (2026-03-01 → 2026-05-31): Vivek will extract and provide a CSV with headers. We will redact IPs and device identifiers unless you confirm they are required.
- Keystore rotation manifest: security will export rotation events and provide a CSV manifest.
- Privileged access review snapshot: CS/Ops will provide PDF copies of the quarterly reviewer checklist signed-by logs.
- Plain-English revocation process doc: I will draft and attach as a short memo.

Two quick asks: 1) Do you need hashes/signatures on the CSVs for chain-of-custody? 2) Any fields we should avoid redacting (user ids, event timestamps are presumably required)?

I'll attach a draft bridge letter for your legal review once the SOC 2 period is confirmed. Vivek — can you confirm retention windows and whether the revocation events include both OAuth token revocation and TOTP disable events?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 artifacts: MFA revocation and keystore rotation evidence

Vanessa / Hannah —

I can take point on the artifact extraction. Notes on availability and format: 

1) MFA revocation events — what we can provide: 
   - CSV: event_time (ISO8601), user_id (hashed if requested), event_type (token_revoked | mfa_disabled | api_key_revoked), auth_method (otp | oauth | webrtc), requester_principal, request_origin (region), request_id.
   - Retention: auth event store retains 12 months; we can extract the requested window (2026-03-01 → 2026-05-31) with no sampling.
   - PII redaction: we will redact IP addresses and device IDs by default, but can provide unhashed user_ids or full IPs with a data transfer agreement.

2) Keystore rotation manifest — what we can provide: 
   - CSV: key_id, rotation_timestamp, previous_key_id, rotation_author (service_account), rotation_reason, kms_provider (cloud-kms / hsm).
   - Note: For HSM-backed keys we will provide the rotation manifest; private key material is never exported.

3) Privileged access review — we can produce PDF snapshots of the signed reviewer checklist for Q1 2026 and the latest reviewer log export.

4) Chain-of-custody: we can supply SHA256 hashes of each artifact file on request and a brief extraction manifest.

Attachments I will push to the secure share (redwood drive):
- mfa_revocation_log_slice_2026-03-01_2026-05-31.csv (redacted IPs)
- keystore_rotation_manifest_2025-12_to_2026-05.csv
- access_review_snapshot_app_admins_202605.pdf
- bridge_letter_draft_pulsehealth.docx (draft)

I will avoid including raw IPs in the CSV we initially share. Hannah — if you confirm that IPs are required for your forensics, state the legal basis and we will route through DPA process.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@pulsehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 artifacts: MFA revocation and keystore rotation evidence

Thanks Vivek — that format looks fine. Two clarifying items from our side: 

1) Token revocation proof: can you include an example revocation event that shows the request_id and the service principal that initiated the revocation? Our compliance team needs to see the linkage between the revocation action and the operator/service. Redacted user_ids are fine if you include a consistent hash so we can correlate.

2) Chain-of-custody: SHA256 per file would be great. Please also include a short note on how the export was generated (script name or internal ticket id).

3) Bridge letter: if the SOC 2 Type II period ends 2026-04-30, we will need a letter covering 2026-05-01 → 2026-06-30 describing interim controls until the next audit or confirmation that no control changes occurred. A draft is fine — our legal will redline.

One more ask: can you remove geolocation from the request_origin column for privacy? Region (us-east/us-west) is sufficient.

If you can send the initial package by EOD today we will start ingestion. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

Hannah
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 artifacts: MFA revocation and keystore rotation evidence

Hannah — attaching the initial package to the secure share and sending a link below. Per Vivek's note, IPs and raw device IDs have been redacted; user_id is presented as a consistent SHA256 hash so you can correlate events without exposing PII. The CSVs include request_id and rotation_author fields where applicable.

Deliverables uploaded:
- pulse_questionnaire_q2_2026.pdf (completed questionnaire)
- mfa_revocation_log_slice_2026-03-01_2026-05-31.csv (redacted IPs, user_id hashed)
- keystore_rotation_manifest_2025-12_to_2026-05.csv
- access_review_snapshot_app_admins_202605.pdf
- redacted_auth_log_sample.txt (small, human-readable sample)
- bridge_letter_draft_pulsehealth.docx (draft bridge letter covering 2026-05-01 → 2026-06-30)
- extraction_manifest_and_hashes.txt (SHA256 hashes for each file)

Secure share: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/PL-5942-pulse-evidence (link sent to pulsehealth security group)

We will wait for confirmation on whether you require unredacted IPs. If so, we will start the DPA routing process and provide a timeline. I can also schedule a 20-min walkthrough with Vivek tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
